title: Long-running task continuity without conversation-memory dependence
failurePattern: A non-human external wait can be mistaken for task completion.
A child task can complete while its parent task is silently forgotten.
Retry count and resume position can disappear when they exist only in conversational context.
A Human stop or approval boundary can be confused with an automatic continuation condition.
designResponse: Persist machine-readable execution state separately from process definition.
Represent return conditions explicitly rather than infer completion from conversational flow.
Re-evaluate the parent after child completion.
Persist blocker identity and retry count.
Give explicit Human interrupt / gate state higher priority than automatic continuation.
limitations: This case does not publish the production Task State schema, storage mapping, recovery implementation, or authority routing.
Passing the public fixture proves the synthetic state-transition contract only, not byte-for-byte identity with private production code or independent authentication of field operation.
